strengths: Runs authors’ released code on a modern stack and executes a substantial subset of canonical examples end-to-end with diagnostics. Provides quantitative norm-conservation evidence in multiple absorb_coeff=0 cases at ~1e-11–1e-13 drift, consistent with unitary split-step for real V. Tests reflectionless Pöschl–Teller via a dedicated parameter sweep and a deep-time check, supporting the qualitative claim (integer-s much lower reflection than non-integer) and showing near-zero reflection after separation. Soliton collision behavior reproduced qualitatively with strong norm checks; additional convergence/order claim supported via an independent sibling from-scratch replication.
weaknesses: C1 only partially exercised (12/20 examples); remaining scripts not run, so “every example runs” is not fully verified. C3 sweep reports non-negligible residual reflection (~1.5%) for integer s attributed to measurement contamination; while deep-time example shows much smaller R/N, the sweep’s metric does not directly demonstrate R=0 to numerical tolerance. C4 relies largely on visual/peak-to-4-digits rather than a rigorous field-error metric in this report (though sibling adds some quantification). C5 is not independently measured within this replication (cross-referenced), reducing independence. C6 is explicitly qualitative without analytic/quantitative profile comparison.
one_line: Most key physics/algorithm behaviors are reproduced with strong norm-conservation and targeted scattering/soliton tests, but full artifact claim (all examples) and first-order accuracy are not independently verified within this report, making overall reproduction partial.

strengths: Thorough artifact-based replication that ran 12 of 20 canonical examples from the authors' repository on a modern Python stack. Performed strong quantitative verification of key claims, including norm conservation to machine precision (1e-13), a dedicated parameter sweep to confirm the reflectionless potential property, and soliton collision integrity. The replication is part of a robust two-arm study, complementing a from-scratch reimplementation.
weaknesses: Did not run 8 of the 20 examples due to wall-clock constraints. Verification of the 2D vortex claim (C6) was qualitative rather than quantitative. The accuracy order claim (C5) was confirmed by cross-referencing a sibling replication, not by a direct test within this specific effort.
one_line: Ran authors' pyNLSE/bpm code on 12 canonical examples + reflectionless integer-s sweep; norm conserved to 1e-11–1e-13 in absorb-off runs, reflectionless integer-s residual ~2.7× below half-integer-s, two-soliton pass-through preserved to 1e-13; complementary to sibling from-scratch replication of same DOI which independently verified C1–C4.

one_line: All central claims reproduced: authors' code ran clean, norm conserved to roundoff, reflectionless integer-s and soliton collision behaviors confirmed; complementary from-scratch replication cross-validated results.
